title: Spot-weld a nickel strip onto a 2x2 pack of 18650 cells with a welder's pen on its lead
instruction: Lay the nickel strip on the battery pack, then spot-weld it to all four cells with the welding pen and put the pen back in its holster.
context: Joining cylindrical cells into a pack is assembly-line and repair-bench work: team assemblers (O*NET 51-2092.00; BLS counts them with other miscellaneous assemblers and fabricators, about 1.47 million US jobs in 2024) rotate through every task of their line. Cells are joined by resistance spot-welding nickel strip onto each terminal with a welding pen on heavy leads from a power unit; in automatic mode the welder fires when both needles are pressed onto the metal at their set force. One hand lays the strip; the other takes the pen, presses it square on each + terminal hard enough to fire without knocking the loose pack, while its lead drags, and puts it back. This builds the idea of TK-PF8K7B (PR #1300, another team's, withdrawn) and does what its review asked: a pen on a heavy lead to a power unit, a stated needle force for each weld, and a loose pack.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the point midway between the two arm bases, which stand 61 cm apart: forward means away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. Battery pack (battery_pack, loose, 201 g): a 2x2 pack of 18 x 65 mm cells (yellow wrap, + up) in a black ABS holder 41.2 mm square, 20 mm pitch, centred 28 cm forward on the centre line; the cells' + caps stand 0.8 mm proud of the holder. Nickel strip (nickel_strip, loose, about 1 g): an H of 0.15 mm nickel, two 8 x 28 mm bars 20 mm apart joined by an 8 mm bridge, with a grip tab folded up from the bridge (8 mm wide, 14 mm tall, 3 mm across), lying in a 40 x 40 mm grey tray (5 mm walls, fixed) 24 cm forward, 17 cm left. Welder power unit (welder_unit, fixed): a bench capacitor spot welder, 14 x 23 x 23 cm, centred 58.5 cm forward, 20 cm right, its display and knobs on the front and, at bench level, the socket its lead's plug sits in (the socket's slot is narrower than the plug). Welding pen (weld_pen, loose, 110 g): 13 cm long, a black grip 24 mm across above a red finger guard 42 mm across, two copper needles 2.5 mm across and 4 mm apart standing 18 mm out of its nose, each on its own spring; it stands in a grey holster cup (fixed, rim 6.7 cm high) 17.6 cm forward, 20 cm right, its guard on the rim. Its lead (weld_lead, 40 cm, 5 mm round, 0.2 kg/m) runs from the socket back along the bench, rises beside the holster and enters the pen's side near its top.
scoring: Defects (0 for the rest of the trial): D1, the pack's centre moved more than 1 cm or tilted over 10 degrees; D2, the pen tilted over 60 degrees (dropped). Strip on the pack: flat (under 10 degrees), resting on the + caps (within 2 mm), its centre within 4 mm of the pack's and its bars within 10 degrees of the pack's axis. A weld on cell k: both needles pushed in at least 1.5 mm (200 g each) at once, both tips within 3.5 mm of the cell's axis and on the strip's top face, the strip on the pack; a welded cell stays welded. Pen home: standing in its holster, its axis within 6 mm of the cup's centre at the rim, guard within 4 mm of the rim, leaning under 12 degrees, after it was taken out. Score: 0.2 strip on, 0.15 per cell welded, 0.1 pen home; 1.0 when all hold, everything is still and both tool points are 4 cm clear, held 1 s (the trial then ends).
reset_notes: Put the strip back in its tray (a fresh strip if it shows weld spots), stand the pack on its mark, stand the pen in its holster with its lead lying back along the bench to the socket. A real trial uses a fresh strip and undamaged cells at storage charge; the welder's mode is automatic, needle pressure set to its lowest (200 g).
fidelity: Rigid bodies and joints, 20 Hz control. The pen's needles are each a slide joint on a spring (1.31 kN/m): 1.5 mm of travel is 200 g. The lead is a chain of 20 capsule links with bending springs (cablekit, as in the accepted cable tasks), plugged into the unit's socket and tied to the pen with a ball joint; each reset lays it from the socket to the pen (cableshape, from an accepted task). A weld is the needles' travel and position: no current, heat or bond. Friction is set so the strip grips the cells' caps harder than the needles grip the strip, as the first weld holds it on a real pack.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (hit the step limit); scripted demo: 1.0
